name: Rhodiola
short: Appeared well tolerated in short-term studies. A volunteer study found modest CYP2C9 inhibition (possibly relevant to warfarin, phenytoin); one case report of serotonergic symptoms with paroxetine.
text: A review of human studies concluded that Rhodiola rosea extract appears to be well tolerated in short-term studies. In a randomised crossover study in 13 healthy volunteers, 14 days of a commercial rhodiola product reduced the activity of the drug-metabolising enzyme CYP2C9 (a 21% decrease in the losartan metabolic ratio) with no significant effect on the other enzymes tested; the authors noted that this modest effect might be clinically relevant for medicines with a narrow therapeutic index that are handled by CYP2C9, such as phenytoin and warfarin. A single case report describes a 68-year-old woman who developed restlessness and trembling, interpreted as a serotonergic syndrome, after adding rhodiola to the antidepressant paroxetine.
